note: What the site renders, where each collection comes from, and where it is served. One declaration, three readers: decision_evals.site hashes `hash` and `site` to gate staleness, site/src/content.config.ts loads `base` and `pattern`, and site/src/lib/remark-rewrite-links.mjs turns `prefix` into `route` so a repository link becomes a site link. Until 2026-08-21 the three restated the globs and a comment asked the next author to keep them in step; two had already drifted. A collection added to one reader and forgotten in another is now a missing field rather than a silent hole. It is not in pyproject.toml because TypeScript cannot read TOML without another dependency.

collections.name: root
collections.why: `hash` is wider than `pattern` on purpose. CLAUDE.md is a byte-identical mirror of AGENTS.md written by `de mirror`, so rendering it would publish one document at two URLs; it is still hashed, because a mirror that moves without a rebuild is a published page disagreeing with the repository. Root documents have no shared prefix, so `rootPages` routes them one at a time.
